disease_label_per_paper: Malignant hyperthermia during anesthesia induction with sevoflurane and succinylcholine for congenital ptosis surgery
presentation_summary: Four-year-old girl with congenital left eyelid ptosis underwent general anesthesia for ptosis surgery.
Preoperative vitals and CK were unremarkable: BP 115/75 mmHg, HR 120/min, RR 18/min, SpO2 100%, temperature 36.7 C, and CK 50 U/L.
Two minutes after sevoflurane and succinylcholine administration she developed tachycardia, masseter contracture, and PETCO2 50 mmHg while temperature remained 36.8 C and SpO2 100%.
Arterial blood gas and labs showed pH 7.17, PaCO2 48 mmHg, PaO2 366 mmHg, bicarbonate 16.7 mmol/L, base excess -10, and CK 10710 U/L, with straw-colored red-tinged urine.
Sevoflurane was stopped, anesthesia was changed to non-triggering agents, she was ventilated with 100% oxygen using a new circuit, and she received dantrolene, hyperhydration, and sodium bicarbonate.
PETCO2 fell, blood gas normalized by 6 hours, she was extubated, and she was discharged on postoperative day 4.
